children: Oil prices extend earlier gains, with Brent crude marching toward $100 a barrel as fresh exchanges of strikes between the U.S. and Iran keep the geopolitical risk premium high. The global oil benchmark is up 1.3% to $97.56 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 1.4% to $92.72 a barrel. "A sustained disruption to actual crude flows could quickly push prices above $100 a barrel," analysts at brokerage firm Kotak Securities. "Tightening inventories and stronger refined-product prices add support." In the U.S., Labor Day weekend travelers are facing the highest gas prices ever for this time of year. According to AAA, the national average price at the pump was $4.15 on Monday, a record high for the holiday. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
